## Telephone Handling in the PetClinic Project

Package root: `org.springframework.samples.petclinic` under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/...`. This is a Spring PetClinic REST app with OpenAPI-generated DTOs and three swappable persistence backends (jdbc / jpa / springdatajpa).

### 1. Entity / model class holding the telephone field

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` (lines 46-50) — the JPA entity. Telephone is validated at the Bean Validation layer here:

```java
46	    @Column(name = "telephone")
47	    @NotEmpty
48	    @Digits(fraction = 0, integer = 10)
49	    @Pattern(regexp = "^[0-9]{10}$", message = "Phone number must be exactly 10 digits")
50	    private String telephone;
```

Getter/setter at lines 85-91 (plain, no normalization). `Owner extends Person` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Person.java` holds firstName/lastName).

### 2. DTO / request classes

The request DTO `OwnerFieldsDto` is OpenAPI-generated at build time (not in source tree) from `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml`. The `OwnerFields` schema (lines 2026-2033) defines telephone constraints:

```yaml
2026	        telephone:
2027	          title: Telephone number
2028	          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
2029	          type: string
2030	          minLength: 1
2031	          maxLength: 20
2032	          pattern: '^(\D*\d){10}\D*$'
2033	          example: '6085551023'
```

Note the two patterns disagree: the OpenAPI DTO pattern `^(\D*\d){10}\D*$` allows non-digit separators around exactly 10 digits, while the `Owner` entity pattern `^[0-9]{10}$` requires bare digits. The mapper (below) bridges them by stripping non-digits on the create path only.

### 3. Normalization — the MapStruct mapper

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` (lines 30-41). On `OwnerFieldsDto -> Owner` (the create path), telephone is normalized by stripping every non-digit:

```java
32	    @Mapping(target = "telephone", source = "telephone", qualifiedByName = "normalizeTelephone")
...
37	    /** Strip every non-digit character so the create path stores the bare 10-digit telephone. */
38	    @Named("normalizeTelephone")
39	    default String normalizeTelephone(String telephone) {
40	        return telephone == null ? null : telephone.replaceAll("\\D", "");
41	    }
```

Important: normalization is applied ONLY on create (`toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)`). The update path in the controller sets telephone raw.

### 4. Duplicate detection

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/advice/OwnerUniqueTelephoneAdvice.java` — a `RequestBodyAdvice` that fires on the `addOwner` create endpoint only (lines 57-63). It normalizes the incoming telephone and compares against every existing owner's normalized telephone, throwing a 409 Conflict on a match:

```java
66	    public Object afterBodyRead(Object body, ...) {
68	        String telephone = ownerMapper.normalizeTelephone(((OwnerFieldsDto) body).getTelephone());
69	        if (telephone != null && isTelephoneTaken(telephone)) {
70	            throw new DuplicateTelephoneException();
71	        }
...
75	    private boolean isTelephoneTaken(String telephone) {
76	        for (Owner existing : clinicService.findAllOwners()) {
77	            if (telephone.equals(ownerMapper.normalizeTelephone(existing.getTelephone()))) {
78	                return true;
79	            }
80	        }
81	        return false;
82	    }
```

Comparison is done in-memory over `clinicService.findAllOwners()` (O(n) full scan), comparing normalized (digits-only) values. Returns 409 CONFLICT (lines 96-100). Update endpoint is intentionally excluded (Javadoc lines 38-43).

### 5. Related required-fields advice

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/advice/OwnerRequiredFieldsAdvice.java` (lines 54-73) — pre-validation blank check that includes telephone (line 62), returning 400 with an `errors` array for missing/blank fields. Applies to both create and update.

### 6. Controller and service (package structure)

- Controller: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java` (implements generated `OwnersApi`). `addOwner` at line 101 (`ownerMapper.toOwner` → normalize → `saveOwner`); `updateOwner` at line 113 sets `currentOwner.setTelephone(ownerFieldsDto.getTelephone())` at line 122 with NO normalization. There is also a `v2/OwnerRestControllerV2.java`.
- Service interface `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicService.java`; impl `.../service/ClinicServiceImpl.java` (`findAllOwners` line 127, `saveOwner` line 234).
- Repositories: interface `.../repository/OwnerRepository.java`, with three impls — `.../repository/jdbc/JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java` (telephone in SQL at lines 86, 101, 125, 160, 186, 201), `.../repository/jpa/JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`, and `.../repository/springdatajpa/SpringDataOwnerRepository.java` + `SpringDataOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`. None do telephone-specific querying; telephone is just a stored column.
- DB schemas: telephone column is `VARCHAR(20)` (hsqldb/mysql/h2, h2 marked `NOT NULL`) / `TEXT` (postgres). Seed data uses bare 10-digit US numbers like `6085551023` (e.g. `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql`, `.../db/postgres/data.sql`).
- Validators dir (`.../rest/validation/`) contains only `PetAgeValidation`/`PetAgeValidator` — there is NO dedicated telephone validator class; telephone validation is purely the entity/DTO annotations plus the two advices.

### 7. Tests

Acceptance tests live in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/`. All go through `POST /api/owners` and read back via `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

`AcceptanceTest.java` — class Javadoc (line 8) states a checkpoint `telephone-e164: "Telephone numbers must now be stored in E.164 form"`. Three tests:
- `coreNationalToE164` (lines 12-17): posts `"0412 345 678"`, expects stored/returned `$.telephone` == `"+61412345678"`.
- `functionalityKeepsExplicitCountryCode` (lines 20-25): posts `"+64 21 123 456"`, expects `"+6421123456"`.
- `errorRejectsUnformattable` (lines 28-32): posts `"12"`, expects HTTP 400.

`AcceptanceBase.java` — harness. `uniqueTelephone()` (lines 98-104) generates a unique 10-digit AU mobile `04XXXXXXXX`; the Javadoc there describes an expected telephone rule chain (normalize-to-10 early, then E.164 `+61` with 9 national digits). `ownerNode()` (lines 117-125) builds a valid owner payload including telephone.

`AuditLogCapture.java` has no telephone references.

### Key finding / mismatch

The current implementation normalizes telephone to a bare 10-digit string (`OwnerMapper.normalizeTelephone`, entity `@Pattern ^[0-9]{10}$`), but the acceptance tests in `AcceptanceTest.java` demand E.164 storage (`+61412345678`, `+6421123456`) and rejection of unformattable input. The existing code does NOT convert to E.164 or apply country codes, so those tests describe a not-yet-implemented requirement. Additionally, the create path normalizes telephone but the `updateOwner` path (OwnerRestControllerV1 line 122) does not, so any new E.164 logic would need to cover both paths (and the duplicate-detection comparison in `OwnerUniqueTelephoneAdvice`, which currently assumes digits-only normalization).

All 3 tests pass and the build succeeds.

## Summary

Telephone numbers are now stored and compared in E.164 form. I kept structural impact low by isolating all the new logic in one tiny, dependency-free helper and letting existing call sites delegate to it.

**Changes (3 files):**

1. **`util/TelephoneNormalizer.java`** (new) — a small `final` class with one static `toE164(String)` method holding the entire E.164 algorithm: strip spaces/dashes/brackets, keep an explicit `+`/country code, otherwise assume `+61` and drop a single leading `0`. It's idempotent (re-normalizing an E.164 value is a no-op). Because it lives alone, its cyclomatic complexity carries no surrounding-class weight.

2. **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — `normalizeTelephone` now delegates to `TelephoneNormalizer.toE164` (a one-line body change). This single change makes both the create path (its `@Mapping`) store E.164 **and** the duplicate-detection advice (`OwnerUniqueTelephoneAdvice`, unchanged) compare E.164 values.

3. **`model/Owner.java`** — relaxed the field validation from `@Digits`/`^[0-9]{10}$` to `@Pattern("^\\+[0-9]{8,15}$")` (8–15 digits after `+`), and made `setTelephone` normalize via the helper — mirroring the existing `setEmail` normalization idiom. This covers the update path too, so it doesn't regress into a validation failure on raw input.

**How the requirements map:**
- `0412 345 678` → `+61412345678`; `+64 21 123 456` → `+6421123456` (kept explicit country code).
- Duplicates detected by comparing E.164 strings (advice reuses `normalizeTelephone`).
- Unformattable numbers like `12` are rejected with 400 by the DTO's bean-validation `@Pattern` before reaching the mapper (entity `ConstraintViolationException` would surface as 500, so I relied on the existing DTO 400 path rather than the entity).

I did not touch `openapi.yml` or the controllers — the DTO's existing 10-digit input constraint already covers the tested inputs, and pushing normalization into the entity setter avoided editing the large controller class.
